correlates.name: Ruptured Chordae Tendineae / Papillary Muscle Dysfunction after Myocardial Infarction
correlates.presentation: the valve leaks severely; the lecturer notes it can leak so far that it produces severe, even lethal cardiac incapacity.
correlates.pathophysiology: low coronary blood flow in MI ruptures a chorda tendinea or paralyzes a papillary muscle. The tethering system fails, so during ventricular contraction the mitral leaflet bulges far backward into the left atrium.

correlates.name: Atrial Fibrillation
correlates.presentation: frequently silent - the lecturer stresses that many people do not realize they have it.
correlates.pathophysiology: irregular, rapid, erratic, non-rhythmic beating of the atria. Coordinated atrial contraction is lost, so the atria cannot deliver the primer-pump volume to the ventricle - exactly the situation in which the normally minor atrial kick becomes important.

correlates.name: Case Study Opened in This Lecture (diagnosis deferred to Part II)
correlates.presentation: 73-year-old man in the ER with exertional dyspnea, syncope and chest pain; poorly managed hypercholesterolemia and an 11-year history of hypertension.

findings.name: JVP 'a' Wave
findings.represents: Atrial contraction — the pressure bump of atrial systole, following the P wave by about 0.1 second
findings.territory: Right atrium, read from the jugular venous pulse
findings.association: Absent in atrial fibrillation; prominent in first-degree AV block; large in right atrial myxoma, pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary stenosis

findings.name: JVP 'c' Wave
findings.represents: Compression of the atrium by the contracting ventricle, appearing just after the peak of the QRS
findings.territory: Right atrium, transmitted from the tricuspid valve bulging backward
findings.association: Marks the start of ventricular systole on the venous tracing

findings.name: JVP 'x' Descent
findings.represents: Atrial relaxation, when atrial pressure falls after contraction
findings.association: Absent in tricuspid regurgitation, where systolic backflow fills the atrium instead of letting it relax

findings.name: JVP 'v' Wave
findings.represents: Passive atrial filling from the great veins while the AV valve is still closed

findings.name: JVP 'y' Descent
findings.represents: The fall in atrial pressure as the AV valve opens and the atrium empties into the ventricle
findings.territory: Right atrium at the onset of ventricular filling
findings.association: Slow in tricuspid stenosis; absent in cardiac tamponade, where the ventricle cannot expand to receive the blood

findings.name: S1 Heart Sound
findings.represents: Closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves at the start of isovolumetric contraction
findings.territory: AV valves, timed to the QRS
findings.association: Marks the beginning of systole; all four valves are closed during the phase it opens

findings.name: S2 Heart Sound
findings.represents: Closure of the aortic and pulmonic valves at the start of isovolumetric relaxation
findings.territory: Semilunar valves, timed just after the T wave
findings.association: Marks the beginning of diastole and end-systolic volume

findings.name: S3 Heart Sound
findings.represents: A low-pitched sound during the rapid filling phase, as blood strikes a compliant or overfilled ventricle
findings.association: Normal in youth and pregnancy; in an older patient it suggests volume overload and heart failure

findings.name: S4 Heart Sound
findings.represents: Atrial contraction forcing blood into a stiff ventricle during atrial systole
findings.association: A stiff, non-compliant ventricle — hypertrophy from long-standing hypertension or aortic stenosis

formulas.name: Normal Chamber Pressures
formulas.equation: LV 100-140 / 3-12; aorta systolic = LV systolic, diastolic ~80; LA mean 2-10; RA mean 2-8 mmHg
formulas.meaning: The pressure map that drives every valve: valves are entirely passive and open or close only because a gradient reverses
formulas.normalValue: Right-sided pressures sit below their left-sided counterparts, and LV and RV outputs equalize over minutes

formulas.name: Cardiac Cycle Timing
formulas.equation: One beat lasts 0.8-0.9 s at 60-100 bpm; two-thirds diastole and one-third systole at rest
formulas.meaning: Atrial systole takes about 100 ms against roughly 800 ms of atrial diastole, and the AV nodal delay of more than 0.1 s exists so the atria can load the ventricles first
formulas.normalValue: With exertion diastole shortens far more than systole, which is why tachycardia compromises filling and coronary perfusion

formulas.name: Atrial Kick
formulas.equation: About 10 mL of a 140 mL end-diastolic volume, up to 20% at most
formulas.meaning: Most atrial blood reaches the ventricle passively during atrial diastole, not during atrial systole — so losing the kick matters only when the ventricle is already stiff or the rate is high
formulas.normalValue: Its loss is what makes new atrial fibrillation symptomatic

formulas.name: The Seven Phases of the Cardiac Cycle
formulas.equation: Atrial systole, isovolumetric contraction, rapid ejection, reduced ejection, isovolumetric relaxation, rapid filling, reduced filling
formulas.meaning: The two isovolumetric phases are the only times all four valves are shut, and they are exactly the flat segments of the ventricular volume curve — if volume is changing, a valve is open
formulas.normalValue: S1 opens isovolumetric contraction; S2 opens isovolumetric relaxation
